Thanks — quick technical note from the SE side.

Short answer: hosted autoscaling can cover short 15 TPS bursts for the model families you mentioned, provided we do a few things up front:
- Warmup: run low‑latency warmup calls ahead of predictable event windows (market open / earnings).
- Cache: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (saves tokens and reduces compute).
- Batching: for non-real‑time portions (backfill or bulk summarization) use batching to reduce unit cost.
- Rate policy: set soft burst limits + fallback model variant (smaller quantized model) to keep latency under SLO during large spikes.

If Finlytics is comfortable with occasional 200–500 ms added latency for fallbacks, hosted should be fine and will be more cost‑efficient. For strict p50/p95 latency targets during sustained 15 TPS we should size a Dedicated pool.

I’ll prepare a short appendix (throughput / latency tradeoffs + recommended endpoint configuration) and drop it in the Drive link Ben shared.

Rishi
